paper.title: Combinatorial Multivariant Multi-Armed Bandits with Applications to Episodic Reinforcement Learning and Beyond

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB-MT (combinatorial MAB with multivariant and probabilistically triggering arms)
unmapped: base arm outcomes are d-dimensional multivariate vectors in [0,1]^d
probabilistically triggered arms (feedback only from triggered set)
general nonlinear reward function satisfying 1-norm MTPM/MTPM+ smoothness
settings.definition_quote: A CMAB-MT problem instance can be described by a tuple $([m], d, \Pi, \cD, D_{\text{trig}},R)$, where $[m]=\{1,2,...,m\}$ is the set of multivariant base arms; $d$ is the dimension of multivariant base arm's random outcome (with bounded support $[0,1]^d$)

settings.name_in_paper: Episodic RL (finite-horizon tabular MDP, unknown transitions) as CMAB-MT
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic tabular reinforcement learning (finite-horizon MDP), not a bandit problem
unmapped: regret over T episodes against optimal value V_1^*(s_1)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the finite-horizon MDP, i.e., episodic MDP, which can be described by a tuple $(\cS, \cA, H, \cP, \cR)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Probabilistic maximum coverage for goods distribution (PMC-GD)
unmapped: each selected node's outcome is multinoulli over |V| targets
settings.definition_quote: The PMC-GD problem is modeled by a weighted bipartite graph $G=(U,V,E,p)$ ... each selected node $u'$ will cover one of its neighbors in $V$, and the edges form a multinoulli distribution ... select at most $k$ nodes in $U$ to maximize the number of covered nodes in $V$.

algorithms.name: CUCB-MT with extended value iteration oracle (Alg. 2)
CUCB-MT with optimistic value iteration oracle (Alg. 3)
CUCB-MT with efficient PMC-GD joint oracle (Alg. 4)

symbols.m_arms: number of base arms (sum_arms ranges over the m base arms)

conditions: satisfies 1-norm MTPM or MTPM+ smoothness with weights in [0,w_bar]^d
concentration events E_c1, E_c2 hold with probability at least 1-1/T

source.label: thm:reg_CMAB-MT
source.quote: if the oracle $\tilde{\cO}$ is an $(\alpha,\beta)$-approximation oracle, and concentration events $\mathcal{E}_{c,1},\mathcal{E}_{c,2}$ hold with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{T}$, then CUCB-MT (Algorithm 1) achieves an $(\alpha,\beta)$-approximate gap-dependent regret bounded by O(...)

results.notes: (alpha,beta)-approximate regret T*alpha*beta*r(pi*) - E sum r(pi_t;mu), defined through expected rewards; recorded as pseudo_regret. Sum over base arms.

symbols.F_bar: upper bound on sum_i q_i F_{t,i}^2
symbols.G_bar: upper bound on sum_i q_i G_{t,i}^2
symbols.K_batch: batch size: max expected number of triggered arms

conditions: satisfies 1-norm MTPM or MTPM+ smoothness with weights in [0,w_bar]^d
concentration events E_c1, E_c2 hold with probability at least 1-1/T

source.label: thm:reg_CMAB-MT
source.quote: and the gap-independent regret bounded by O\left(\sqrt{m(\bar{F}+\bar{G})T}+m(\bar{I}+\bar{J})\log (KT)\right).

results.notes: (alpha,beta)-approximate regret. For CMAB-T with Bernoulli arms yields O~(B1 sqrt(mKT)) (Remark 5).

source.label: thm:reg_RL_loose
source.quote: CUCB-MT algorithm with the confidence region function $\cC_t$ in \cref{eq:RL_loose_conf_set} and the joint oracle in \cref{alg:ext_VI} satisfies the requirements of \cref{thm:reg_CMAB-MT} with parameters $\bar{F}=\tilde{O}(H^3S),\bar{G}=\bar{I}=\bar{J}=0$, and thus achieves a regret bounded by $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{H^4S^2AT})$.

results.notes: Appendix proof also gives O(sum_{s,a,h} H^3 S log(SAHT)/Delta^min) gap-dependent and O(sqrt(H^4S^2AT log(SAHT))). Regret is sum of V^*-V^{pi_t}, expected values. Horizon set not_applicable (RL); confidence uses T.

source.label: thm:reg_RL_tight
source.quote: CUCB-MT algorithm (\cref{alg:CUCB-MT}) with the confidence region function $\cC_t$ in \cref{eq:RL_conf_set_tight} and the joint oracle in \cref{alg:v-opt} achieves a regret bounded by $O(\sqrt{H^3SAT\log (SAHT)}+H^3S^2A\log^{3/2} (SAHT))$

results.notes: Matches Omega(sqrt(H^3SAT)) up to logs. Appendix also gives gap-dependent O(sum H^2 L/Delta^min + sum H^2 S L^1.5 log(1/Delta^min)) as by-product (not separately stated as a theorem).

symbols.k_sel: number of selected source nodes (batch size)

source.label: thm:reg_PMC_GD
source.quote: For PMC-GD equipped with pseudo-reward in \cref{eq:pseudo_reward}, CUCB-MT algorithm ... satisfies the requirements of \cref{thm:reg_CMAB-MT} with parameters $\bar{F}=\tilde{O}(k|V|)$, $\bar{G}=\bar{I}=\bar{J}=0$, and thus achieves a $(1-1/e,1)$-approximate regret bounded by $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{k|U||V|T})$.

results.notes: (1-1/e,1)-approximate regret. Appendix: O(sqrt(k|V||U|T log(|U||V|T))) and gap-dependent O(sum_u k|V|log(|U||V|T)/Delta_u^min).
